paragraphs: Hyman identifies this designation with R’ Abba bar Manyumi, as in Sanhedrin 17b and Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 6:8. The Arukh, under dan, transcribes Rav Adda bar Manyumi.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The consulted Sanhedrin 17b text reads Rav Adda bar Minyomei, matching the type of variant Hyman attributes to the Arukh. His Rabbi Abba reading remains visible.

The consulted Sanhedrin 17b paragraph names Rav Adda bar Minyomei. Two whole paragraphs in the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 6:8 text expressly mention the judges of Nehardea, supporting the collective designation; they do not themselves name Abba or Adda. Hyman’s identification and the Arukh wording remain his report, without a fresh Arukh-witness collation. His abbreviated Abba title is retained as R’.
